title: Cost law under output mapping
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, fix a learning-access mode, and let $f\colon\alpha\to\beta$. For any Boolean target function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube and any program with output in $\alpha$, running the program with its output mapped by $f$ has the same law as mapping each run's output by $f$ while leaving its learning cost unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean target function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube is given
A program with output in $\alpha$ is given
